items.title: First aid Treatment for Dislocation and Sprain

source_refs.note: First aid Treatment for Dislocation and Sprain: a main subheading of 12.2 Disorders of the skeletal system, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 272-273.

blocks.text: First aid treatment for dislocation and sprain includes the following steps (Fig. 12.18):

items: Immobilize the affected area: Keep the affected area immobile and do not attempt to re-align the dislocated joint. Use a sling or splint to support the limb.

blocks.alt: Four numbered pictures: 1 Immobilize the affected area (gloved hands bandage an injured ankle, and a woman wears an arm sling); 2 Apply ice (a hand holds an ice pack on a knee); 3 Elevate the affected limb (a man lies with the injured arm and the bandaged leg raised on pillows); 4 Seek medical attention (a doctor puts a hand on a patient's shoulder in a hospital).
blocks.caption: Figure 12.18: First aid treatment for dislocation or sprain (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.18).

items: Apply ice: Apply an ice pack or cold compress to the affected area to reduce swelling and pain.
Elevate the affected limb: In the case of dislocation, if possible, elevate the affected limb above to help reduce swelling.
Seek medical attention: Dislocations and sprain require medical attention, so call for emergency medical services 1122 or take the person to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment.
